newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan tightens credit limits as stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan tightens credit limits as stocks rise.

text.p: The Taiwan stock market's rise above 8,400 points on Monday has triggered anti-speculation regulations under which regulators will tighten credit trading limits from Tuesday, authorities said.
Taiwan Stock Exchange Corp, the island's main bourse, said margin-buying and short-selling ratios would be trimmed by 10 percentage points each to 40 and 50 percent, respectively.

To avoid excessive credit expansion at the time of sharp stock market rallies, the exchange has benchmarks to reduce credit trading limits when the index passes 6,000, 7,200, 8,400 point and 9,600 points, officials said.
"Now that the index has passed 8,400, the credit trading limits will be cut by 10 percent from tomorrow," an official told Reuters by telephone.
The weighted index advanced 135.11 points or 1.63 percent to close at its intra-day high of 8,426.42, a six-year high.

According to rules, the margin-buying ratio or margin loan ratio -- the degree to which securities finance firms can lend to investors for buying shares -- would fall to 40 percent of a share's purchase price from 50 percent.

The short-selling or stock-loan ratio -- margin requirements for shares investors can borrow from securities finance firms for short selling -- would be reduced to 50 percent of a share's selling price from 60 percent.
The exchange has said the rules are aimed at limiting financial risks and "preventing the stock market from overheating."
